Great demo earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so procurement/security has what they need:

Security/credentials we discussed:
- Preferred: service-account JWTs exchanged for short-lived tokens (recommended for regulated data).
- Alternatives: OAuth client-credentials or scoped API keys with rotation.

Attachments: integration-diagram.png (high level), atlas-soc2.pdf (SOC2 evidence you asked about).

1) Redwood provisions a sandbox project and a sample SDK repo (Node + Python) with short-lived JWT flow.
2) We demo key rotation and automated token refresh in a 20–30m follow-up.
3) Atlas to confirm procurement/security contact list and required rotation cadence (30/90/180 days).

Can you confirm the rotation cadence and whether you want us to demonstrate KMS-backed key management (we support Vault/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault + HSM options)?

Thanks — I cc'd Ben to scope the credential playbook and Monica for the SDK handoff.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration & credentialing — sandbox and next steps after demo

Hi Alice — quick answers and a proposed minimal viable credential pattern: 

1) Rotation & short-lived tokens: yes — Redwood supports short-lived access tokens (recommended). Typical pattern we use for enterprise: a long-lived service account credential (stored in customer KMS/Vault) -> a token exchange on our control plane returns a 1-hour access token to the SDK. We support rotating the long-lived service account key every 90 days; the control plane will revoke issued tokens on key rotation.

2) BYOK & KMS: supported. We have integrations for GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and AWS KMS/HSM. Customers can either upload encrypted key material or configure KMS to sign/assert.

3) Audit logs: we can stream token issuance/revocation and per-request metadata to your SIEM (Syslog/HTTPS/CloudPubSub). We include request id, model, route, token_id in the log.

Proposed MVP for the sandbox demo:
- Provision Atlas sandbox project with two routes: /embed and /rerank and one tool-call route for claims.
- Provide a sample SDK (node/python) that does: service-account JWT -> POST /v1/token-exchange -> receive 1h access token -> call inference routes.
- Show key rotation: rotate long-lived key in KMS, demonstrate revocation and re-issuance.

I've attached a short credential-playbook.md that walks through the flows and includes sample curl commands and config for Vault/KMS.

Available slots for the 30m demo: Tue 6/19 10:00am PT or Wed 6/20 2:00pm PT. Which works?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
